description: Real court decisions and official rules on validity of reservation certificates (OBC-NCL, EWS, SC/ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen, domicile) in Indian government recruitment. Research data only; not consumed by any engine yet. See certificate_cases.README.md.

cases.case_name: Divya v. Union of India & Ors.

facts.notes: Held only an I&AC for FY 2019-20 on the cut-off date; FY 2020-21 certificate obtained on 2023-06-01.

cases.rule_applied: CSE-2022 Rules 13, 27(3), 28 read with DoPT OMs 19.01.2019 and 31.01.2019: I&AC for FY 2020-21 must be possessed by the closing date.
cases.outcome_note: Candidature converted from EWS to General; writ petition dismissed.
cases.quote: the I&AC must be as per the prescribed norms and must be in possession of the candidate on or before the cut-off date.

cases.case_name: Vimlok Tiwari & Ors. v. UPSC (petitioner 2: Ashwani Dubey), decided with Divya v. Union of India

facts.notes: Tehsildar later (2023-01-16) certified the FY 2021-22 entry was a mistake for 2020-21; clarification produced after DAF-I deadline.

cases.rule_applied: I&AC must state the correct FY (2020-21) and be possessed by the closing date; post-deadline corrections not accepted.
cases.outcome_note: Converted to General category; writ petition dismissed.
cases.quote: The UPSC was justified in rejecting the claim of the petitioners, for consideration under the EWS Category in CSE-2022.

cases.case_name: Union Public Service Commission v. Gaurav Singh & Ors. (respondent-writ petitioners 2 and 4)
cases.case_number: C.A. No. 4152 of 2022 arising out of SLP (C) No. 426 of 2021; (2024) 2 SCC 605
cases.recruitment: UPSC Central Armed Police Forces (AC) Examination 2019

facts.notes: Certificates dated after the last date and for the later FY; High Court noted a one-time relaxation requiring certificates dated earlier than 01.08.2019.

cases.rule_applied: DoPT OM 31.01.2019 paras 4.1 and 5.3: income for FY prior to year of application; crucial date is the closing date.
cases.outcome_note: High Court order set aside as regards writ petitioners 2 and 4.
cases.quote: they have filed certificates issued subsequent to the last date and for the later financial year.

cases.case_name: Union Public Service Commission v. Gaurav Singh & Ors. (respondent-writ petitioner 1)
cases.case_number: C.A. No. 4152 of 2022 arising out of SLP (C) No. 426 of 2021; (2024) 2 SCC 605
cases.recruitment: UPSC Central Armed Police Forces (AC) Examination 2019

facts.notes: Correct date and FY; only defect was a seal stamped without the officer's name.

cases.rule_applied: A seal/format irregularity not attributable to the candidate does not defeat a certificate of the correct date and FY.
cases.outcome_note: Directed to be treated as an EWS candidate (writ petitioner 3, issuing-authority objection, also accepted).
cases.quote: The certificate of writ-petitioner No.1 was also accepted as there was no discrepancy in either the date of issuance or the year.

cases.case_name: Poonam Dwivedi & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors. (appellant Poonam Dwivedi)
cases.case_number: C.A. arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 4001-4002 of 2023 (2026 INSC 351)

facts.notes: Certificate for FY 2020-21 was issued before that FY closed; valid window per Court was 01.04.2021 to 05.01.2022.

cases.rule_applied: UP OM 18.02.2019 / Clause 8.3 of advertisement: income for FY prior to year of application, certificate issued by last date of application.
cases.outcome_note: Appeals dismissed; exclusion from EWS select list upheld.
cases.quote: were issued prior to even closure of the relevant financial year, there was an error apparent on the face of those certificates

cases.case_name: Poonam Dwivedi & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors. (appellant Sunita Kumari)
cases.case_number: C.A. arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 4001-4002 of 2023 (2026 INSC 351)

facts.notes: Certificate related to FY 2021-22 instead of 2020-21 (also dated after the last date of application).

cases.rule_applied: Certificate of a different FY goes to the root of eligibility (following UPSC v. Gaurav Singh).
cases.outcome_note: Appeal dismissed.
cases.quote: even the certificate of Sunita Kumari was invalid for claiming the benefit of reservation.

cases.case_name: Poonam Dwivedi & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors. (appellant Archana Saxena)
cases.case_number: C.A. arising out of SLP (C) No. 20256 of 2023 (2026 INSC 351)

facts.notes: Certificate stated valid for FY 2020-21 but income was for FY 2019-20; quote is the High Court Division Bench finding reproduced and upheld by the Supreme Court.

cases.rule_applied: Income must be for the FY prior to the year of application (2020-21).
cases.outcome_note: Appeal dismissed.
cases.quote: though, it was required to be filed for the financial year 2020-21, thus, this certificate is not valid.

cases.case_name: Poonam Dwivedi & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors. (appellant Shanu Tiwari)
cases.case_number: C.A. arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 4001-4002 of 2023 (2026 INSC 351)

facts.notes: Income for FY 2019-20, certificate stated valid for 2020-2021; quote is the High Court Division Bench finding upheld by the Supreme Court.

cases.rule_applied: Income must be for the FY prior to the year of application (2020-21).
cases.outcome_note: Appeal dismissed.
cases.quote: This certificate too did not relate to the financial year

cases.case_name: Sakshi Arha v. The Rajasthan High Court & Ors.
cases.case_number: C.A. No. 3957 of 2023 with connected appeals (2025 INSC 463)
cases.recruitment: Rajasthan High Court Civil Judge Examination 2021 (advertisement 22.07.2021)

facts.notes: OBC-NCL / MBC-NCL appellants; each held only older certificates (2012-2018) without affidavit and fresh ones issued in 2022. Subsequent notice of 04.08.2022 fixed the 31.08.2021 cut-off.

cases.rule_applied: Where advertisement is silent, eligibility is judged on the last date of application; Rajasthan circulars 09.09.2015 / 08.08.2019: NCL certificate valid one year, extendable to three years with affidavit.
cases.outcome_note: Appeals dismissed; split verdict of 18.05.2023 resolved against the candidates.
cases.quote: none of the appellants had a valid certificate and/or accompanied by the affidavit as per the proforma at the relevant time

cases.court: Supreme Court of India (3-Judge Bench), affirming Rajasthan High Court order dated 18.08.2022
cases.case_name: Jyoti Beniwal v. The Rajasthan High Court (decided with Sakshi Arha v. The Rajasthan High Court)
cases.case_number: C.A. No. 3909 of 2023 (arising from D.B. Civil Writ Petition No. 11784 of 2022) (2025 INSC 463)
cases.recruitment: Rajasthan High Court Civil Judge Examination 2021

facts.notes: Presented an OBC-NCL certificate of the year 2016.

cases.rule_applied: OBC-NCL status is determined annually; certificate must be valid as on the last date of application.
cases.outcome_note: Writ petition dismissed by High Court; appeal dismissed by Supreme Court.
cases.quote: the certificate of the year 2016, as presented by the petitioner therein, was deemed to have failed to meet the requirements as per the law

cases.case_name: Aashima Goyal v. Union of India & Anr.

facts.notes: Submitted FY 2018-19 I&AC; FY 2017-18 I&AC submitted only on 24.09.2020 after the extended deadline of 31.08.2020; family income for FY 2017-18 also found above Rs 8 lakh via CBDT.

cases.rule_applied: DoPT OMs 19.01.2019 and 31.01.2019: income for FY 2017-18 (AY 2018-19) below Rs 8 lakh, certificate by deadline.
cases.outcome_note: Candidature cancellation (09.09.2020) upheld; writ petition dismissed.
cases.quote: was not able to meet the extended deadline fixed for submission of the correct I&A certificate for the F.Y. 2017-18

cases.case_name: Deepak Kumar v. Airports Authority of India & Ors.
cases.recruitment: Airports Authority of India recruitment (EWS category)

facts.notes: Did not produce the FY 2023-24 certificate at document verification; undertaking to submit by 06.02.2026, last extension 13.02.2026.

cases.rule_applied: Recruitment notice prescribed FY 2023-24 income and asset certificate; no relaxation clause.
cases.outcome_note: Writ petition dismissed; candidature cancellation upheld.
cases.quote: Relying upon a certificate of any other financial year will not validate the reservation claimed by the petitioner
cases.uncertain_reason: Judgment date not stated in the fetched report (report published 15 May 2026); judgment PDF not read.

cases.case_name: Kadam Kiran Sanjay v. Indian Coast Guard
cases.recruitment: Indian Coast Guard Navik (General Duty) 01/2025 batch

facts.notes: Submitted FY 2023-24 certificate; also held FY 2024-25 certificate issued 11.04.2024. Notice required documents issued on/before 03.07.2024 and valid until 30.04.2025.

cases.rule_applied: DoPT OM 31.01.2019 (FY preceding year of application); ambiguous advertisement notes construed for the candidate.
cases.outcome_note: Disposed in terms of interim order of 16.04.2025; petitioner inducted and allowed to continue.
cases.quote: an EWS certificate pertaining to the financial year preceding the year of application cannot be rejected merely on a technical ground

cases.case_name: Raghvendra Singh & Anr. v. Union Public Service Commission & Anr.

facts.notes: Rule 21.2 required OBC-NCL certificates issued 01.04.2024-14.05.2024 (2024 exam) or 01.04.2023-16.05.2023 (2023 exam); lead petitioners' certificates fell outside the window.

cases.rule_applied: Rule 21.2 of CAPF (AC) Examination Rules held arbitrary; DoPT OM 08.10.2015 (provisional appointment on prima facie proof).
cases.outcome_note: Certificates outside the window to be accepted, subject to verification of OBC-NCL status.
cases.quote: to cancel the candidature of otherwise eligible candidates, on sole grounds of issuance date, deprives the petitioners of their fundamental rights
cases.uncertain_reason: UPSC stated (in W.P.(C) 3404/2025) that it intended to appeal to the Supreme Court; appeal status not checked.

cases.case_name: Bharath Singarappa v. Union Public Service Commission & Ors.

facts.notes: Notice window 01.04.2023-16.05.2023; held NCL certificate dated 16.02.2023 and another issued February 2024.

cases.rule_applied: Followed Raghvendra Singh v. UPSC (2025:DHC:11105-DB).
cases.outcome_note: Candidature to be considered subject to verification; seniority but no financial benefits.
cases.quote: the cut off date shall not be a factor for disqualification

cases.case_name: Amjad Khan v. The Chairman, Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board & Ors.
cases.recruitment: DSSSB Advertisement No. 02/2012, TGT (Maths) Male, Post Code 110/12

facts.notes: Applied for OBC certificate on 14.06.2012 and enclosed the receipt; certificate issued 28.06.2012; same certificate accepted for his LDC selection.

cases.rule_applied: Ram Kumar Gijroya (2016) 4 SCC 754; DoPT OM 08.10.2015; Sakshi Arha distinguished (application pending with competent authority).
cases.outcome_note: CAT order set aside; consideration for appointment with notional seniority, no back salary.
cases.quote: Procedural requirements must yield to substantive justice where the eligibility of a candidate is otherwise established and undisputed.

cases.case_name: Karn Singh Yadav v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi & Ors.
cases.case_number: C.A. arising out of SLP (C) No. 14948 of 2016 (2022 INSC 1031)
cases.recruitment: MCD 'A' Grade Staff Nurse, advertisement dated 30.08.2007

facts.notes: OBC documents not filed before the cut-off date.

cases.rule_applied: Ram Kumar Gijroya v. DSSSB (2016) 4 SCC 754.
cases.outcome_note: Held covered by Ram Kumar Gijroya, but no substantial relief granted given lapse of time.
cases.quote: The instant matter is thus completely covered by said decision.

cases.case_name: Rajat Ghosh v. Tripura University
cases.recruitment: Tripura University, Associate Professor (Pharmacy), OBC-NCL reserved post

facts.notes: Selected candidate (respondent 7) obtained the updated OBC-NCL certificate after the interview and selection; advertisement required eligibility by the last date.

cases.rule_applied: DoPT OMs 08.10.2015 and 29.03.2023 (provisional consideration on prima facie proof); Sakshi Arha distinguished as arising under Rajasthan rules.
cases.outcome_note: Appeal against the appointment dismissed.
cases.quote: permitted production of the caste certificate at a later date in spite of the advertisement saying that it should be produced before the cut-off date

cases.case_name: Union of India & Ors. v. Rohith Nathan & Anr., etc.
cases.case_number: C.A. Nos. 2827-2829 of 2018 with connected appeals (2026 INSC 230)

facts.notes: Creamy-layer status computed by DoPT from salary of parents employed in PSU/private sector (para 9 of letter 14.10.2004), where equivalence with Government posts was not established.

cases.rule_applied: OM 08.09.1993 Income/Wealth Test excludes salary income; letter 14.10.2004 para 9 discriminatory without equivalence.
cases.outcome_note: Union's appeals dismissed; candidates satisfying NCL criteria to be accommodated (supernumerary posts) within six months.
cases.quote: Thus, we find no infirmity in the judgments impugned before us.

cases.court: High Court of Punjab and Haryana (Division Bench)
cases.case_name: Divya Kalia v. State of Haryana

facts.notes: SC certificate lacked registration number/date in the prescribed position; Tehsildar confirmed it genuine.

cases.rule_applied: Possession of eligibility vs proof (Charles K. Skaria; Dolly Chhanda; Ram Kumar Gijroya): defects attributable to the issuing authority may be condoned.
cases.outcome_note: Rejection quashed; costs on HPSC.
cases.quote: the fault (if any) was solely the competent authority concerned in issuing the SC certificate

cases.case_name: Letters Patent Appeals arising from W.P.(S) No. 3151 of 2018 batch (JPSC/JSSC recruitments)
cases.recruitment: JPSC and JSSC recruitments (Dentist (Basic Cadre), police radio operator and others)

facts.notes: Candidates uploaded central-government format caste certificates or produced state-format certificates only at document verification after the cut-off date.

cases.rule_applied: Advertisement required caste certificate details in the prescribed State format before the last date; Ram Kumar Gijroya held inapplicable.
cases.outcome_note: Treated as general category; appeals dismissed.
cases.quote: can be treated under the general category if they fail to submit details of caste certificates in the prescribed format before the application deadline
cases.uncertain_reason: Report gives only 'Ranchi, May 7' without year or case number; lead appellant name not stated.

cases.court: Central Administrative Tribunal, Principal Bench, New Delhi
cases.case_name: Samit Kumar v. Union of India (DoPT) & Ors.

facts.notes: Disability certificate (Mental Illness - BPAD, benchmark >40%) was temporary, valid up to 03.11.2026; rejected 14.05.2025 relying on DEPwD clarification 20.01.2025.

cases.rule_applied: RPwD Act 2016 s.2(r) and RPwD Rules 2017 r.18(3); DoPT OM 17.05.2022 held confined to promotion.
cases.outcome_note: Rejection quashed; appointment subject to AIIMS Medical Board reassessment.
cases.quote: a valid benchmark disability certificate cannot be disregarded merely because it specifies a period of validity

cases.case_name: Shritij Mohan Shrivastava v. Reserve Bank of India & Anr.
cases.recruitment: RBI Officers in Grade 'B' (DR) - General, advertisement dated 10.09.2025

facts.notes: Permanent disability certificate and UDID (60%, Autism Spectrum Disorder with Learning Disability); advertisement required permanent certificate issued before closing date.

cases.rule_applied: Government of India notification 04.01.2021 identifying ASD(M), MI and MD as suitable; RPwD Act Schedule.
cases.outcome_note: RBI directed to issue appointment order.
cases.quote: the petitioner additionally having a learning disability, in our opinion, certainly cannot be considered to be any ineligibility

cases.case_name: Ghunna Ram v. Union of India & Ors.

facts.notes: Serving Havildar Major applied as ESM with serving-personnel certificate showing completion of service by 31.12.2020; UPSC said he was not discharged within one year of the last date of application.

cases.rule_applied: Rule 5(c)(i), Ex-servicemen (Re-employment in Central Civil Services and Posts) Rules 1979 as amended 2012: assignment due to be completed within one year, counted from declaration of results.
cases.outcome_note: Cancellation quashed; to be processed against an available ESM vacancy, no arrears.
cases.quote: the benefit of any ambiguity has to enure to the benefit of the candidate, and not the administration.
cases.uncertain_reason: Judgment date not stated in the fetched report; LiveLaw weekly round-up places it around 16-22 March 2026.

cases.court: High Court of Madhya Pradesh (Single Judge)
cases.case_name: Aakansha Meena v. State of M.P.
cases.recruitment: MP Police Subedar (M.P. Police Executive (Non-Gazetted) Service Recruitment Rules 1997)

facts.notes: Domicile certificate issued after the last date of application; advertisement required it only for age-relaxation claimants and the form had no domicile column.

cases.rule_applied: Requirement not in advertisement/application form cannot be inserted by a later notice.
cases.outcome_note: Writ petitions allowed; permitted to participate in second stage.
cases.quote: the respondents could not have denied the petitioner's participation in the second stage of the selection process

rules.reference: O.M. No. 43011/11/2022-Estt.(Res-II) dated 19.09.2022 (FAQ 15), restating O.M. No. 36039/1/2019-Estt(Res) dated 31.01.2019 para 4.1
rules.rule: Family gross income (all sources) below Rs 8 lakh for the financial year prior to the year of application.
rules.quote: Income for the purpose shall include income from all sources i.e. salary, agriculture, business, profession, etc. for the financial year prior to the year

rules.reference: O.M. No. 43011/11/2022-Estt.(Res-II) dated 19.09.2022 (FAQ 21), restating O.M. dated 31.01.2019 para 5.3
rules.rule: Crucial date for the Income & Asset Certificate is the closing date for receipt of applications unless the advertisement fixes another date.
rules.quote: may be treated as the closing date for receipt of application for the post, except in cases where crucial date is fixed otherwise.

rules.rule: A certificate issued after the crucial date and for a later financial year is a major discrepancy.
rules.quote: Income & Asset Certificates issued subsequent to the crucial date and for the later Financial Year shall be treated as major discrepancies.

rules.rule: Worked example: closing date 1 August 2022 -> income FY 2021-22, certificate valid for 2022-23. A blank validity year with the correct FY in the body may be referred back to the issuer.
rules.quote: the financial year for computing gross annual income of the family shall be 2021-2022 and the certificate shall be valid for 2022-2023.

rules.rule: SC/ST and Central-List OBC persons are not eligible for EWS in Central Government posts; a State-list-only OBC may obtain an EWS certificate.
rules.quote: Applicants belonging to SC, ST or OBC included in the Central List residing in any of the States/UTs are not eligible for EWS reservation

rules.rule: Creamy layer income limit Rs 8 lakh per annum (Category VI of Schedule to O.M. 08.09.1993); test applied over three consecutive years.
rules.quote: It has now been decided to raise the income limit from 6 lakh to 8 lakh per annum for determining the creamy layer

rules.reference: O.M. No. 36033/1/2013-Estt.(Res.) dated 13.09.2017 (recital of O.M. No. 36012/22/93-Estt.(SCT) dated 08.09.1993)
rules.rule: Creamy layer is judged on gross annual income for a period of three consecutive years.
rules.quote: for a period of three consecutive years would fall within the creamy layer

rules.rule: A SC/ST/OBC candidate unable to produce the prescribed certificate may be appointed provisionally on prima facie proof, subject to furnishing the certificate within a reasonable time.
rules.quote: he/she may be appointed provisionally on the basis of whatever prima-facie proof he/she is able to produce in support of his/her claim

rules.reference: Sakshi Arha v. Rajasthan High Court, 2025 INSC 463, para 27 (following Bhupinderpal Singh (2000) 5 SCC 262)
rules.rule: Eligibility date: recruitment rules first, then advertisement; if both are silent, the last date for submission of applications.
rules.quote: in case of absence of specifications in both context, the eligibility is to be adjudged in lieu of the last date of submission of applications

rules.issuer: Government of Rajasthan, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (circulars 09.09.2015 and 08.08.2019), as applied by the Supreme Court
rules.reference: Sakshi Arha v. Rajasthan High Court, 2025 INSC 463, para 33
rules.rule: Rajasthan OBC/MBC-NCL certificate valid one year from issue, extendable up to three years with an affidavit.
rules.quote: is valid for a period of one year from the date of issuance, and subsequently, extendable up to three years
rules.uncertain_reason: Official circular text read only as reproduced in the judgment; original circular not fetched.

rules.reference: Bir Singh v. Delhi Jal Board, decided 30.08.2018, para 30 (Ranjan Gogoi J.)
rules.rule: SC/ST status is tied to the State/UT of the Presidential Order; a migrant cannot claim SC/ST benefits of the State to which he migrates (State services).
rules.quote: cannot be deemed to be a Scheduled Caste person in relation to any other State to which he migrates

rules.reference: Bir Singh v. Delhi Jal Board, decided 30.08.2018, para 61 (majority)
rules.rule: For NCT of Delhi services the pan-India reservation rule (SC/ST of any State) is valid.
rules.quote: so far as the National Capital Territory of Delhi is concerned the pan India Reservation Rule in force is in accord

rules.reference: Ex-servicemen (Re-employment in Central Civil Services and Posts) Amendment Rules, 2012, dated 04.10.2012, rule 5(c)
rules.rule: For All India Competitive Examination posts (Group A/B), ESM with five years' service released on completion of assignment, including those whose assignment is due to be completed within one year, get up to five years' age relaxation.
rules.quote: on completion of assignment (including those whose assignment is due to be completed within one year)

rules.reference: O.M. No. 36035/8/2023-Estt.(Res-II) dated 19.05.2023, as reproduced in the RBI Grade B advertisement quoted in Shritij Mohan Shrivastava v. RBI (Bom HC, 05.08.2026)
rules.rule: Reservation in permanent jobs should not be granted on a temporary disability certificate (contested: CAT in Samit Kumar held a valid time-bound certificate cannot be ignored).
rules.quote: not be appropriate to grant the benefit of reservation in jobs which are permanent in nature on the basis of temporary certificate of disability
rules.uncertain_reason: Official O.M. not fetched; text read only as reproduced in an advertisement inside the judgment.

rules.issuer: Ministry of Home Affairs (CAPF (AC) Examination Rules 2023, Rule 21.2)
rules.reference: Reproduced in Raghvendra Singh v. UPSC, Delhi HC, 10.12.2025, para 7
rules.rule: CAPF (AC) 2023 required OBC-NCL certificate on FY 2022-23/2021-22/2020-21 income, issued on/after 01.04.2023 and not later than the closing date. Delhi HC declared this window arbitrary.
rules.quote: issued on/after 01.04.2023 (after completion of FY 2022-23) but not later than the closing date of the application
rules.uncertain_reason: Rule struck down by Delhi HC; Supreme Court appeal status not checked.
